brief: Wilson had argued that clearing two weeks of event risk, hyperscaler earnings then midterms, would allow a year-end rally led by the biggest stocks, and that an AI sentiment pendulum oversold since end-Q2 was creating opportunities again; he calls the past two weeks bruising for that view. He still holds the AI investment cycle as the dominant driver of macro markets. Three things learned this week: hyperscaler cloud growth is accelerating (Alphabet, Azure, AWS revenue and backlog growth), with management citing 85% of global IT spend still on-premises as runway, so the ROI question is being answered; financing fears have eased (Meta's equity raise, Oracle's pulled-forward breakeven and $20bn financing need, stable capex plans, four straight weeks of falling 10-year yields), so the financing gap is less feared than a week ago; and a bull market in cyber risk is emerging after the Binance heist. Separately, the market is trading unprecedented correlation breakdowns and a stalled AI-winners-vs-laggards trade even as the Nasdaq sold off over 3.5% on Intel and software concerns. Wilson argues AI demand isn't slowing, supply is the binding constraint, the 2007/2008 financing analogy is wrong (1997-vs-1999 is the better frame), and capex-demise fears look exaggerated.
